results.title: 17-year-old charged with murder over killing of Ghanaian teenager Javits Frimpong in New York
results.content: A 17-year-old has been charged with murder in connection with the fatal shooting of 15-year-old Ghanaian boy Javits Frimpong in the Bronx, New York. The New York Police Department (NYPD) said detectives arrested the suspect on Wednesday morning and took him to the 42nd Precinct for questioning before charging him with murder. Javits was shot in the stomach near Crotona Park on October 29, 2026. Police officers rushed him to St. Barnabas Hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The suspect's identity has not been released because he is a minor. The NYPD says it is still searching for other people who may have been connected to the shooting. Javits' father, Thomas Frimpong, said he was relieved that a suspect had been charged. Speaking emotionally at a press conference on Wednesday, he recalled that he was at work when he received news that his son had been shot.

results.title: Kojo Brace officially declares intention to contest NPP parliamentary primaries in Ahanta West
results.content: Former JoyNews presenter Samuel Kojo Brace has declared his intention to contest the New Patriotic Party (NPP) parliamentary primary in the Ahanta West constituency of the Western Region. Brace announced that he had formally submitted his expression of interest to the party's National Elections Directorate on Friday, November 6, 2026. In a video shared on his official Facebook campaign page, The Ahanta Pele, he thanked supporters for their encouragement and advice throughout the process. “Thank you for the continued support, the love, the critique, the advice, and the prayers. They have indeed shaped the journey over the past months,” he said. He added that his decision followed consultations with constituents and NPP members in the constituency.

results.title: ENNY Foundation wins award for autism advocacy and special needs support
results.content: The ENNY Foundation has received the Paragon of Autism Advocacy and Special Needs Excellence award at the fifth edition of the Eminent Awards, in recognition of its work supporting children with diverse learning needs and promoting inclusive education. The award was presented on October 31, 2026, at the National Theatre in Accra during the awards' fifth anniversary celebration, known as the Quintessence Edition. According to the foundation, the recognition reflects years of work providing intervention and support for children and families, training parents, teachers and caregivers, and promoting more inclusive learning environments. The citation traced the foundation's beginnings to the volunteer work of its founder, Emmanuel Ntow Nyarko, who worked with children requiring additional educational support before establishing ENNY as a platform for intervention, training and advocacy.
